chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, both of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whenever the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) sent out a military expedition, he would call its commander, seat him by his side, and seat his companions before him; then say: 'March in the name of God, and with God, and in the way of God, and upon the religion of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). Do not be treacherous, do not steal from the spoils, do not mutilate, and do not cut down a tree unless you are compelled to. Do not kill a decrepit old man, nor a child, nor a woman.' And whichever man, from the lowest to the most excellent of the Muslims, grants protection to any of the polytheists, he is under protection until he hears the word of God. When he hears the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: if he follows you, he is your brother in your religion; and if he refuses, seek God's assistance against him and deliver him to his place of safety.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly, except that he said:
And whichever man from the Muslims grants protection to a man from the polytheists — whether in the farthest part of the army or its nearest — he is under protection.

key_terms.جار: Jar — one who has been granted temporary protection (aman); inviolable until he reaches safety
key_terms.سريّة: Sariyya — a military expedition or detachment sent without the Prophet personally leading it
key_terms.غلول: Ghulul — treacherous appropriation of war booty before its distribution; a grave sin
key_terms.كلام الله: Kalam Allah — the word/speech of God (i.e., the Quran), recitation of which gives the person a chance to accept Islam
key_terms.مأمن: Ma'man — place of safety/security to which an enemy combatant must be escorted if he declines Islam
key_terms.مثلة: Muthla — mutilation of a corpse; strictly prohibited in Islamic law
key_terms.مِلَّة: Millah — religion, creed, or religious community

ai.seo_question: What instructions did the Prophet Muhammad give before sending a military expedition according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) transmission of the Prophet's (SAWW) standing orders when dispatching military expeditions. The Prophet would personally brief the commander, emphasizing divine authorization for the mission while enumerating strict prohibitions: no treachery, no looting, no mutilation, no destruction of trees, and no killing of non-combatants (the elderly, children, and women). A second chain via Ali ibn Ibrahim provides a slightly variant wording. These instructions reflect the Islamic laws of war (jihad rulings) and show that even the humblest Muslim soldier could grant temporary safe-passage (aman) to an enemy until that person heard the Quran recited.
